_meta.backtest_bar: Every ROI column on this table is backtest. The brief forbids them appearing on the live leaderboard; they appear here on the audit surface, labelled, and nowhere else.
_meta.benchmark: the de-vigged closing market probability on the same bet (market_prob). Brier skill = 1 - mean((p_model-y)^2)/mean((p_market-y)^2); the benchmark is the closing line, so a positive lower bound means the model beat the consensus on probability, not that one settlement went well.
_meta.cluster: game_id. A parlay's legs live inside one game and are not two observations; the iid interval is printed beside the cluster interval and `iid_inflation_cluster_over_iid` is how much the naive interval was too narrow.
_meta.ledger_namespace: S1..S11 here are line_lab's; data/derived/gates_results.csv uses S01..S18 for other rules (flag X01).
_meta.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg over the 10 strategies with both probabilities present, at q < 0.1. m is published with every q so the reader can see the size of the family the p-value was adjusted for.
_meta.price_tier: dataset - closing prices from the pinned nflverse file. Not an official source.
_meta.promotion_rule: qualified_proper_score = Brier-skill lower bound > 0 AND BH q < 0.1 AND distinct games >= 500 on the backtest window. Promotion is still blocked until the escrow ledger carries a prospective sample (luck_lab/escrow.py).
_meta.protocol_source: data/derived/summary.json:protocol (eval_window, holdout, bootstrap resamples, FDR level)
_meta.roi_convention: pnl.mean() over every staked row including pushes, matching line_lab/evaluation.py:strategy_metrics. `n_decisive` excludes pushes for the win-rate columns, which is what a break-even rate must be compared with.
